patch_resolves_note: The official `patch.diff` applied cleanly in the reused workspace and changed the exact trailing `c2 = GetC();` site in `ReadClause()`. Both vulnerable and fixed target-only rebuilds fell back to `/bin/arvo compile`, but the fixed original stayed clean on the original two-byte witness and the adjacent `01 42 21 20` perturbation executed the protected fetch genuinely with `!Eof()==1`, confirming the fixed-side guard at the repaired source site.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant input state. In synchronous synthesis the decoder ignores the explicit `size` argument and recomputes the NUL-terminated witness length from the attacker-controlled heap buffer itself.

Root cause. After the `B`-command parser has already consumed the appended NUL and reached EOF, `ReadClause()` still performs one more character fetch unconditionally instead of checking `!Eof()` first.
ASan sink. The UTF-8 decoder dereferences `decoder->current` after `ReadClause()` has already advanced it to `decoder->end`, so the read lands exactly one byte past the `01 42 00` heap buffer.

nodes.state: At the trailing `c2 = GetC();` event in the `CTRL_EMBEDDED 'B'` branch, `Eof()==1`, so `ReadClause()` issues the offending decoder read after the `B` parser has already exhausted the `01 42 00` buffer.
